rules.title: California statewide annual rent increase cap (5% + CPI, max 10%)
rules.requirement: An owner of covered residential real property may not, over any 12-month period, raise the gross rental rate by more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower. The cap is measured from the lowest gross rental rate charged in the 12 months before the increase takes effect, excluding accepted owner-offered discounts, incentives, concessions or credits. For a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains in lawful possession, the owner may set the initial rate. The cap applies only to later increases. The rate and any discounts must be separately listed in the lease or amendments. Section 1947.12 is operative April 1, 2024 and is repealed as of January 1, 2030 by its own terms.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.key_value: 5% plus CPI change, capped at 10% (whichever is lower) per 12 months
rules.exemptions: Section 1947.12(d) does not apply to: (1) housing deed- or agreement-restricted as affordable, or subject to affordable-housing subsidy agreements; (2) dormitories owned and operated by a higher education institution or a K-12 school; (3) housing under valid local rent or price control that restricts annual increases to less than subdivision (a); (4) housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless it is a mobilehome; (5) separately alienable property whose owner is not a REIT, a corporation, an LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, and whose tenants received the statutory written exemption notice; (6) a two-unit single structure where the owner occupies one unit as principal residence at the start of the tenancy and continues in occupancy, and neither unit is an ADU or JADU. Subdivision (j) also excludes a homeowner of a mobilehome.
rules.interaction: The section expressly does not expand or limit local governments' authority to regulate rents under Civil Code Chapter 2.7 (§ 1954.50 et seq.). Housing under a local rent control that restricts annual increases to less than subdivision (a) is exempt. The text also references just-cause provisions in § 1946.2 for the owner exemption notice; those provisions are not in this chunk.

rules.title: California limit of two rent increases per 12 months for a continuing tenant
rules.requirement: Where the same tenant remains in occupancy of a covered unit over any 12-month period, the gross rental rate may not be increased in more than two increments over that period. Increases remain subject to the other restrictions of subdivision (a), including the overall cap.
rules.quoted_span: the gross rental rate for the unit of residential real property shall not be increased in more than two increments over that 12-month period
rules.key_value: Maximum 2 increments per 12-month period (same tenant in occupancy)
rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the annual cap under § 1947.12(d) and (j): affordable or subsidized housing, dormitories, locally rent-controlled housing with a lower cap, housing with a certificate of occupancy within 15 years (other than mobilehomes), qualifying separately alienable property with notice, an owner-occupied two-unit property (no ADU or JADU), and mobilehome homeowners.
rules.interaction: This limit applies together with the percentage cap in subdivision (a)(1) and does not replace it. The section is repealed as of January 1, 2030 by its own terms.
